title: Australia Council Amendment (Creative Australia) Bill 2023
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications and the Arts

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill updates the Australia Council Act 2013 to put parts of the National Cultural Policy into effect by 1 July 2023.
It would let the Council operate as 'Creative Australia', take over the work of Creative Partnerships Australia Ltd, and run new functions for arts workplaces and music.
The bill also removes Creative Partnerships as a body that can receive tax-deductible donations for the Australian Cultural Fund.
changes: The Council may use the name 'Creative Australia'.
The Council takes on the functions of Creative Partnerships Australia Ltd, including its assets, liabilities, staff and records.
Creative Partnerships Australia Ltd is abolished.
The bill updates constitutional limits so the Council can fund constitutional corporations.
The Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 is amended to stop Creative Partnerships being a Deductible Gift Recipient for the Australian Cultural Fund.
summary.affected: The Australia Council, Creative Partnerships Australia Ltd, and arts organisations and practitioners.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Five bills were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration: the Migration Amendment (Australia's Engagement in the Pacific and Other Measures) Bill 2023, the Migration (Visa Pre-application Process) Charge Bill 2023, the Australia Council Amendment (Creative Australia) Bill 2023, the Royal Commissions Amendment (Enhancing Engagement) Bill 2023, and the Treasury Laws Amendment (2023 Measures No. 1) Bill 2023.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Hanson-Young
speeches.brief: The Greens supported the Australia Council Amendment (Creative Australia) Bill 2023 as a first step but argued it must be backed by substantial funding, criticising the previous government's "Brandis cuts" and calling for arts to be prioritised over stage 3 tax cuts and nuclear-powered submarines. The speaker highlighted the Adelaide Fringe Festival's million-ticket sales and insisted every child deserves access to art and music classes.
